I hadn't yet decided what I would do once I had returned, but circumstances had conspired to force a choice upon me. Should I protect these helpless villagers by attacking the bandits or should I help the bandits keep these peasants in their place? No doubt my actions here will dictate the future of the land.

This is the beginning of something new...something good. I went against my upbringing and attacked the bandits to protect the peasants. I've started something here, and I must finish the job: I must kill all attacking bandits and save the village, and not lose my life doing so.

Otomo was right - Shinja intends to put up a fight. If I destroy his Keep and confront him, he should listen to reason - I am the heir to the Serpent empire, after all. My new clan lacks leadership, though, and will certainly crumble if I were to die.

With Shinja's mercenaries out of the way, he has nowhere left to run. If we destroy his Keep to the North and defeat him, our hunt will end. He's still loyal to my family, so if I live through this battle he'll most certainly join us.
Shinja's mercenaries again...this rabble should fall easily. If I kill them all, this province will join my cause. If I survive, the Clan will grow.

Shinja has always had a talent for escape, but we've cornered him now - that snake doesn't have anywhere else to run. If we defeat him in battle, I can surely sway him to our cause. I must survive if we're to enlist his aid.

The Wolf miners...I never thought I'd be fighting against them. As much as it pains me, we have no choice but to fight - we should clear them away and move on to the Swan's Pool. The Geisha trust me, so I must survive if we're to reclaim the Orb.

The keys to claiming this province are the two villages. I expect some kind of encounter in the second, given the guard's warnings about the Lotus. A display of power will sway the people here, but I mustn't get careless and die if we're to reclaim the Orb from the Geisha.

So, it would seem that this Vetkin is behind all of this...I hope Lord Garrin is all right. I've no idea why the noble Wolf Clan would side with Vetkin, but we must clear them away and move on to the Swan's Pool. The Geisha trust me, so it's imperative that I survive this encounter.

The Lotus...I've never trusted them, and it seems my suspicions were well-founded. If we're to free this province, we'll need to defeat the Master Warlock who controls the locals. The Geisha trust me, so I must be on my guard if we're to reclaim the Orb...
Our enemies have come for the Serpent's Orb - how did they know it was here? Regardless, we must protect the Geisha’s home at all costs if we're to earn their trust and claim the Orb.

The Wolf Clan have changed much while I was away - they're certainly stronger than before. As much as it pains me, we must defeat them and hurry to Serpentholm - the Orb is in danger of falling into the wrong hands.

The Lotus Clan has always had a problem with Serpent authority. The only way to protect my people is to completely wipe them out, leaving neither man nor mortar standing. I cannot fail - we're getting too close.

Many battles have been fought on these grounds, but none so fierce as this. As this will be the new seat of the Dragon Clan's republic, we must leave no trace of the opposition or we compromise the Clan's security forever.

I've never understood Kenji's soft spot for the Wolf Clan - I suppose they're easier to like if you've been vacationing for the last seven years. If our new clan is to flourish, we must wipe out the Wolf Clan and leave none of their hovels standing. We can now build a Keep to house our Zen Masters, so protecting our leaders is no longer crucial to victory.

You can take the Wolf out of the mines, but I guess you can't take the mines out of the Wolf. There are three mines here and we should destroy all of them. They've also built a Cairn at some "nexus" to the East, which will also need to fall. We can now build a Keep to house our Zen Masters, so protecting our leaders is no longer critical.

The Lotus are shaping up to be quite the adversary. I'm sure that even Kenji would agree that they all must be taught a lesson - we'll wipe out all of their people and buildings and move on. We can now build a Keep to house our Zen Masters, so protecting our leaders is no longer essential.

I never remembered this province being so desolate. I know we're getting close, and it's not because of the smell of burning flesh. The Dragon is here, waiting for me at the spire...I just know it. I must meet with him - perhaps his power is the key to ending this war.

The Dragon has issued a challenge - I must brave the gauntlet of the Dragon's Spire and meet it at the mountain's summit. This trial is sure to be difficult, but if I survive I'll have the Dragon's favor.

Betrayed! I should have seen this coming. There's a village to the East which can provide us with supplies and a work force. If we gain their support we should have no problem wiping out the Lotus and returning to Serpentholm and punishing those responsible.

The traitor Shinja must be defeated! He's resurrected the old Serpent guard, built himself a fine Keep and allied himself with the Lotus - all must fall. Shinja will pay for what he did to you, Otomo!

The Ninja are bound by the mysterious Soul Flame...if we destroy its pedestal to extinguish the flame, they'll be bound to us. We're not prepared to build a town here, so we must use our forces carefully.

The Lotus have allied with the Ninja and would prevent me from allying with the Monks. If we destroy the Lotus outpost and weather the Ninja's attacks we will be victorious, provided that the Monastery is still standing.
This is the last province before we arrive on the Lotus home plateau. Obliterating the Lotus here is the only option.
Zymeth is using the orb, no doubt - if we besiege his forces he should show himself. Once we kill Zymeth, this should all be over...

The Horde, the Dragon Clan's legendary foe, still lives and comes to infest our land. If we survive their attacks long enough it should draw out their leader, this "Nightvol." Killing that monster is our goal.
These Peasants need to learn their place and serve as an example to others that might rebel. If I kill them all and survive the encounter, the Serpent Clan will live on.
Shinja was always a little too headstrong for his own good. If I tear down his keep and I survive, surely he'll come to his senses and join me.

A good general always has an escape route ready, and Shinja is certainly a good general. Fortunately, we've cornered him here. If we tear down his keep, defeat him in combat and I'm alive after it all, he'll have no choice but to join me...or die.

Poor Otomo, fighting his never-ending battle for what is "right." Well, that ends today - if we defeat all of his hired mercenaries and confront him, surely he'll join me and help rebuild the Serpent empire. Slaughtering these weaklings should be amusing, but I mustn't get get carried away and lose my life.

Shinja has nowhere to run - if we defeat him, surely he'll come to his senses and service the Serpent Clan once again. Shinja and Otomo have always fought, so I'll have to stay alive to keep them in their places.

I used to respect the Wolf Clan, but now they're starting to annoy me. If we destroy their town and kill all of them, they should think twice before interfering with the Serpent Clan again. It's imperative that I stay alive if we're to reclaim the Orb from the Geisha.

There are two towns here just waiting to submit. I expect a scuffle with the Wolf Clan, but a display of power is the only way we'll win this province over. I need to survive if we're to get anywhere with the Swan's Pool Geisha.
It's time Garrin's "sense of justice" got the better of him. If we crush his town and kill him, that should be just the kind of example we need to sway this province to our side.

I'm not sure why Father trusted the Lotus, but we're all paying for it now. If we kill them and crush all of their buildings we can move on. The Geisha won't trust Shinja or Otomo, so I'll have to survive this encounter if we're to gain their support.
The Swan's Pool Geisha need protection yet again - if we're to get the Orb from them, we'll need to protect them from the Lotus onslaught and earn their trust.
These flea-bitten miners make such terrible use of their freedom. If we destroy their towns and kill the rabble, surely they'll take note of the Serpent's power.
The Lotus and their feeble tricks sicken me - kill them all and raze their towns and we can move on to Serpentholm.
I can't remember a more glorious battle on these hallowed grounds - kill, raze and maim all that stand in our way and the seat of Serpent power will be secured once again!

The Wolf Clan have moved to the forefront of our battle. We must decimate their forces and towns and reclaim this province as our own. We can now build a Keep to house our Zen Masters, so the clan can press on if I am injured.

This farce has gone on long enough. If we destroy their three shale mines and their place of magic, the Cairn, we can break the back of the Wolf Clan resistance. We can now build a Keep to house our Zen Masters, so the clan can press on if I am injured.

The Lotus's original treachery took place in this decrepit province, and it will be their final resting place - leave no man or building standing! We can now build a Keep to house our Zen Masters, so the clan can press on if I am injured.

I'm not the superstitious type, but something is wrong here. This area was said to be home to a benevolent Dragon, but something...darker is here now. My gaze is continually drawn to the top of the spire, and I believe I'll find some answers there. I must survive.

This Necromancer will be a powerful ally, indeed - enemies that die in his presence are immediately recruited to our service as undead warriors. We have no peasants to build a town, but the Necromancer's powers should suffice to wipe out Otomo's pitiful rebels.
The traitor Otomo must die, as must his pathetic Wolf allies. Otomo is nowhere to be seen now, but he is sure to emerge if we slay enough of his friends.

So the Wolf want to enlist the Ninja's aid, do they? If we protect the Soul Flame from the Wolf the Ninja should join us instead. Or...we could probably catch the Ninja unprepared and destroy the Soul Flame first...
With the Ninja on our side, it's time we eradicated the remaining Wolf forces.

These petulant Monks just don't know when to stop. If we demolish their precious monastery, we should have no trouble crushing their spirits and "convincing" them to join our cause. We can't build a town, but our starting forces should be adequate.
This one province stands between me and Grayback. Liquidate the Wolf forces here and we'll be on our way.

The rebel Grayback is breathing his last breaths. Attacking his forces should draw him from the Keep. If we kill him the pathetic Wolf Clan will dissolve and we can recover the Serpent's Orb at long last.
If we fight this abominable swarm of Hordelings their leader is sure to appear. Once this "Nightvol" reveals itself, we must kill it to complete our subjugation of this land.

I hadn't yet decided what I would do once I had returned, but circumstances had conspired to force a choice upon me. Should I protect these helpless villagers by attacking the bandits or should I help the bandits keep these peasants in their place? No doubt my actions here will dictate the future of the land.

This is the beginning of something new...something good. I went against my upbringing and attacked the bandits to protect the peasants. I've started something here, and I must finish the job: I must kill all attacking bandits and save the village, and not lose my life doing so.

Otomo was right - Shinja intends to put up a fight. If I destroy his Keep and confront him, he should listen to reason - I am the heir to the Serpent empire, after all. My new clan lacks leadership, though, and will certainly crumble if I were to die.

With Shinja's mercenaries out of the way, he has nowhere left to run. If we destroy his Keep to the North and defeat him, our hunt will end. He's still loyal to my family, so if I live through this battle he'll most certainly join us.
Shinja's mercenaries again...this rabble should fall easily. If I kill them all, this province will join my cause. If I survive, the Clan will grow.

Shinja has always had a talent for escape, but we've cornered him now - that snake doesn't have anywhere else to run. If we defeat him in battle, I can surely sway him to our cause. I must survive if we're to enlist his aid.

The Wolf miners...I never thought I'd be fighting against them. As much as it pains me, we have no choice but to fight - we should clear them away and move on to the Swan's Pool. The Geisha trust me, so I must survive if we're to reclaim the Orb.

The keys to claiming this province are the two villages. I expect some kind of encounter in the second, given the guard's warnings about the Lotus. A display of power will sway the people here, but I mustn't get careless and die if we're to reclaim the Orb from the Geisha.

So, it would seem that this Vetkin is behind all of this...I hope Lord Garrin is all right. I've no idea why the noble Wolf Clan would side with Vetkin, but we must clear them away and move on to the Swan's Pool. The Geisha trust me, so it's imperative that I survive this encounter.

The Lotus...I've never trusted them, and it seems my suspicions were well-founded. If we're to free this province, we'll need to defeat the Master Warlock who controls the locals. The Geisha trust me, so I must be on my guard if we're to reclaim the Orb...
Our enemies have come for the Serpent's Orb - how did they know it was here? Regardless, we must protect the Geisha’s home at all costs if we're to earn their trust and claim the Orb.

The Wolf Clan have changed much while I was away - they're certainly stronger than before. As much as it pains me, we must defeat them and hurry to Serpentholm - the Orb is in danger of falling into the wrong hands.

The Lotus Clan has always had a problem with Serpent authority. The only way to protect my people is to completely wipe them out, leaving neither man nor mortar standing. I cannot fail - we're getting too close.

Many battles have been fought on these grounds, but none so fierce as this. As this will be the new seat of the Dragon Clan's republic, we must leave no trace of the opposition or we compromise the Clan's security forever.

I've never understood Kenji's soft spot for the Wolf Clan - I suppose they're easier to like if you've been vacationing for the last seven years. If our new clan is to flourish, we must wipe out the Wolf Clan and leave none of their hovels standing. We can now build a Keep to house our Zen Masters, so protecting our leaders is no longer crucial to victory.

You can take the Wolf out of the mines, but I guess you can't take the mines out of the Wolf. There are three mines here and we should destroy all of them. They've also built a Cairn at some "nexus" to the East, which will also need to fall. We can now build a Keep to house our Zen Masters, so protecting our leaders is no longer critical.

The Lotus are shaping up to be quite the adversary. I'm sure that even Kenji would agree that they all must be taught a lesson - we'll wipe out all of their people and buildings and move on. We can now build a Keep to house our Zen Masters, so protecting our leaders is no longer essential.

I never remembered this province being so desolate. I know we're getting close, and it's not because of the smell of burning flesh. The Dragon is here, waiting for me at the spire...I just know it. I must meet with him - perhaps his power is the key to ending this war.

The Dragon has issued a challenge - I must brave the gauntlet of the Dragon's Spire and meet it at the mountain's summit. This trial is sure to be difficult, but if I survive I'll have the Dragon's favor.

Betrayed! I should have seen this coming. There's a village to the East which can provide us with supplies and a work force. If we gain their support we should have no problem wiping out the Lotus and returning to Serpentholm and punishing those responsible.

The traitor Shinja must be defeated! He's resurrected the old Serpent guard, built himself a fine Keep and allied himself with the Lotus - all must fall. Shinja will pay for what he did to you, Otomo!

The Ninja are bound by the mysterious Soul Flame...if we destroy its pedestal to extinguish the flame, they'll be bound to us. We're not prepared to build a town here, so we must use our forces carefully.

The Lotus have allied with the Ninja and would prevent me from allying with the Monks. If we destroy the Lotus outpost and weather the Ninja's attacks we will be victorious, provided that the Monastery is still standing.
This is the last province before we arrive on the Lotus home plateau. Obliterating the Lotus here is the only option.
Zymeth is using the orb, no doubt - if we besiege his forces he should show himself. Once we kill Zymeth, this should all be over...

The Horde, the Dragon Clan's legendary foe, still lives and comes to infest our land. If we survive their attacks long enough it should draw out their leader, this "Nightvol." Killing that monster is our goal.
These Peasants need to learn their place and serve as an example to others that might rebel. If I kill them all and survive the encounter, the Serpent Clan will live on.
Shinja was always a little too headstrong for his own good. If I tear down his keep and I survive, surely he'll come to his senses and join me.

A good general always has an escape route ready, and Shinja is certainly a good general. Fortunately, we've cornered him here. If we tear down his keep, defeat him in combat and I'm alive after it all, he'll have no choice but to join me...or die.

Poor Otomo, fighting his never-ending battle for what is "right." Well, that ends today - if we defeat all of his hired mercenaries and confront him, surely he'll join me and help rebuild the Serpent empire. Slaughtering these weaklings should be amusing, but I mustn't get get carried away and lose my life.

Shinja has nowhere to run - if we defeat him, surely he'll come to his senses and service the Serpent Clan once again. Shinja and Otomo have always fought, so I'll have to stay alive to keep them in their places.

I used to respect the Wolf Clan, but now they're starting to annoy me. If we destroy their town and kill all of them, they should think twice before interfering with the Serpent Clan again. It's imperative that I stay alive if we're to reclaim the Orb from the Geisha.

There are two towns here just waiting to submit. I expect a scuffle with the Wolf Clan, but a display of power is the only way we'll win this province over. I need to survive if we're to get anywhere with the Swan's Pool Geisha.
It's time Garrin's "sense of justice" got the better of him. If we crush his town and kill him, that should be just the kind of example we need to sway this province to our side.

I'm not sure why Father trusted the Lotus, but we're all paying for it now. If we kill them and crush all of their buildings we can move on. The Geisha won't trust Shinja or Otomo, so I'll have to survive this encounter if we're to gain their support.
The Swan's Pool Geisha need protection yet again - if we're to get the Orb from them, we'll need to protect them from the Lotus onslaught and earn their trust.
These flea-bitten miners make such terrible use of their freedom. If we destroy their towns and kill the rabble, surely they'll take note of the Serpent's power.
The Lotus and their feeble tricks sicken me - kill them all and raze their towns and we can move on to Serpentholm.
I can't remember a more glorious battle on these hallowed grounds - kill, raze and maim all that stand in our way and the seat of Serpent power will be secured once again!

The Wolf Clan have moved to the forefront of our battle. We must decimate their forces and towns and reclaim this province as our own. We can now build a Keep to house our Zen Masters, so the clan can press on if I am injured.

This farce has gone on long enough. If we destroy their three shale mines and their place of magic, the Cairn, we can break the back of the Wolf Clan resistance. We can now build a Keep to house our Zen Masters, so the clan can press on if I am injured.

The Lotus's original treachery took place in this decrepit province, and it will be their final resting place - leave no man or building standing! We can now build a Keep to house our Zen Masters, so the clan can press on if I am injured.

I'm not the superstitious type, but something is wrong here. This area was said to be home to a benevolent Dragon, but something...darker is here now. My gaze is continually drawn to the top of the spire, and I believe I'll find some answers there. I must survive.

This Necromancer will be a powerful ally, indeed - enemies that die in his presence are immediately recruited to our service as undead warriors. We have no peasants to build a town, but the Necromancer's powers should suffice to wipe out Otomo's pitiful rebels.
The traitor Otomo must die, as must his pathetic Wolf allies. Otomo is nowhere to be seen now, but he is sure to emerge if we slay enough of his friends.

So the Wolf want to enlist the Ninja's aid, do they? If we protect the Soul Flame from the Wolf the Ninja should join us instead. Or...we could probably catch the Ninja unprepared and destroy the Soul Flame first...
With the Ninja on our side, it's time we eradicated the remaining Wolf forces.

These petulant Monks just don't know when to stop. If we demolish their precious monastery, we should have no trouble crushing their spirits and "convincing" them to join our cause. We can't build a town, but our starting forces should be adequate.
This one province stands between me and Grayback. Liquidate the Wolf forces here and we'll be on our way.

The rebel Grayback is breathing his last breaths. Attacking his forces should draw him from the Keep. If we kill him the pathetic Wolf Clan will dissolve and we can recover the Serpent's Orb at long last.
If we fight this abominable swarm of Hordelings their leader is sure to appear. Once this "Nightvol" reveals itself, we must kill it to complete our subjugation of this land.

Our cruel taskmaster, Budo, has refused to feed his workers for many days. We must not let him starve us, or we won't have the strength to rebel against our masters! Budo claims he'll give us a sack of rice if we break some shale for him. We'll see if he lives up to his promises.
I had hoped to plan out our liberation more than this, but my hand has been forced; the time is now. We'll start our rebellion by freeing all of the slaves in this part of the mines.

Budo set us up, and now we're the target of Yvaine's limitless ire. This certainly complicates things - escaping from the deep mines will not be easy. All of this must wait, though...I'd best break down this shale pile before Yvaine changes her mind and kills us.

It's good to have Longtooth at my side again - we'll need his strength as we fight for liberation. Magic barriers and other obstacles stand in our way, but we must reach the other side of this part of the mines. The air is cleaner here and there's a faint smell of trees...freedom is near!

That witch and her cursed magicks! I've been trapped here, alone...at least my men escaped safely. There's another exit around here somewhere, so it's just a matter of finding it. I've never been in this part of the mines before, but if Yvaine's here I expect she'll be attended by plenty of Lotus warriors. I'm sure there are more slaves nearby, and I'll need their help if I'm to succeed.

I've escaped from the mines, much to the relief of my fellow Wolves. Just in time, too - we're under attack by Lotus troops! Fortunately, Longtooth is waiting nearby with reinforcements. If our Pitch Slinger signals from the tower above, Longtooth will see his flames and join forces with us. Then we can take the fight to Yvaine herself...

The snow continues unabated. Even Gaihla's Sanctuary, known for its hot springs, has frozen over. Utara and her Witches are attacking Gaihla's Druidesses and Dryads. We must protect Gaihla's people and defeat Utara, or all is lost - we can set up a town on the western terrace.

We must hold out until Grayback returns. This invisible laboratory must be hiding Gaihla. With just the two of us, though, things are going to be tricky. If we push boulders and destroy enough buildings, surely the commotion will delay the town's disappearance.
Wildeye has done well, but I hope that we're not too late. Gaihla is trapped inside that abominable laboratory, and it's up to us to tear it down and remove her from its twisted confines.

After her ordeal in Soban's Laboratory and the long trek through the blizzard, Gaihla is in bad shape. There's an abandoned monastery to the west where she can rest safely. We'll take shelter in the monastery until she recovers, and then press on towards Yvaine's stronghold. Be wary...Wildeye suspects a trap.

At the monastery, we met a half-monk, half-ninja named Tao. He spoke strangely, but I don't think he's any crazier than Wildeye - for what that's worth! Tao claims that if we defeat the sorcerors Issyl and Koril, we'll be able to walk right through Yvaine's magical barriers. We may as well trust him. After all, what choice do we have?

Our progress has been halted by Taro - a spoiled, soft-minded brat if I ever met one. Unfortunately, he's also the heir to the Serpent Empire, so killing him isn't an option. Good thing he's a coward. Without his father's elite guards, I expect he'll run straight home to Daddy. There are three Royal Academies producing these guards, and we'll need to destroy them all...

The end of our struggle is near. Yvaine's Keep is at the top of the mountain, protected by more of those accursed magical barriers. If we destroy the towns surrounding her Keep, the barriers should fall. Then we'll need to tear apart the Keep itself...and settle our feud with Yvaine, once and for all.
How fitting that this campaign would end in a cave. After I kill Yvaine, this will all be over. I can smell her fetid presence through the dense, frozen air, but something's different about it...

Surprise the Wolf Clan from the side in this swampy province, weakening them on other fronts.
Collapse the flea-ridden Wolf Clan’s shale mines to deprive them of materials for their armories.
The last bastion of Lotus forces have retreated to this province. If we annihilate the Lotus Clan here we permanently scrub them from the political landscape.

Without them, we'll starve when winter comes!

He stays locked up in that house of his and sends Vetkin to do his dirty work.

I will be your guide as you reacquaint yourself with your homeland.
Much has changed since you left and the road to restoration will be long indeed.
Someone awaits your arrival in the clearing to the North.
Let's meet them and start rebuilding your empire.
Before we can move, we'll have to select Kenji.
Now that he's selected, Right-click where you want him to go and he'll walk there.
If you want to unselect Kenji, Left-click something else or Left-click the ground.
This was once peaceful Issen village.
It used to be one of our most beautiful towns, but the Lotus destroyed it five years ago.
This Peasant, Sperri, has been waiting for your return.
He's eager to serve you and rebuild his town.
Sperri can only build the buildings you see at the bottom of the screen.
As you can see, he can only build a Peasant Hut right now.
Left-click on the Peasant Hut icon, then place the hut by right-clicking somewhere on the ground.
If you decide you don't want to build the Hut right now, Left-click to cancel or to select something else.
You can only build on relatively flat terrain, so plan carefully, my Lord.
Remember, Left-click always selects and Right-click always performs actions.
To continue building the hut, select your Peasant and Right-click on the framework we've already started.
Look!  A new peasant has emerged from the hut we built.
Peasants appear from within the huts automatically.
Your village can only support a certain number of people at a time, indicated in the lower left corner of the screen.
Also, the bigger your current population is the slower the Peasant birthrate will be.
If you watch the bar at the bottom left of the screen, you can tell when the next peasant will arrive.
When the bar is full, a Peasant will appear.
Do you see the golden Peasant button in the center interface?
This is the Idle Peasant button.
It will help you keep our Peasants busy and productive.
Left-clicking it will focus on an idle peasant and automatically select him.
If we're to grow, your people will need more food, my lord.
Whenever we construct a building or train a soldier we'll need food and drink to fuel the effort.
Let's harvest some rice from this rice field over here.
Let's select all of our Peasants.
Move the cursor near the Peasants.
Press and hold the left mouse button.
As you move the mouse, you will see a box expand from the cursor.
Drag the cursor until the box encompasses all of the Peasants.
Release the mouse button and the Peasants will be selected.
You can select any of your people in this manner.
This will be crucial to commanding your army effectively, so learn it well.
Now, scroll to the rice field and Right-click on one of the rice plants in the field.
This will tell the Peasants to start harvesting, and they will continue to do so until told differently.
Rice is important, but our people will also need fresh water to drink.
A pond or stream like this one should do nicely.
Select our Peasants, then scroll to the pond and Right-click it.
We're almost ready to start building our army!
To train warriors, we'll need a Dojo.
Notice the Dojo is now available in the build menu.
We'll find a good spot and build the Dojo just like we built the Peasant Hut.
The more peasants we have selected the faster our new Dojo will be completed.
Also, if you hold the right mouse button down and drag left and right we can rotate the building.
When you let go of the button, the building will be placed.
My lord, we must complete our Dojo.
Select some Peasants and Right-click on the Dojo you started to complete it.
Now we'll train our first warrior, a Spearman.
Training a Spearman will cost you rice and water.
Uh oh! We're out of rice!
And look, the fields are dry!
Don't worry, my lord - we can harvest more rice if we water the field.
Select some peasants like we did before.
In the lower right corner of the build interface you'll see the blue Water Rice icon.
Left-click the Water Rice icon, and Right-click one of the depleted rice plants.
In no time the field will be ready for harvesting again - go ahead and tell a Peasant to harvest rice.
Well done! The fields are fertile again and our rice stores have been replenished.
Looks like we'll need some more water, though.
Select a Peasant and order him to harvest some water for us, my lord.
Now, back to training that Spearman…
Select a peasant and Right-click on the Dojo.
This will command the Peasant to enter and train in that building.
Your first soldier will be ready soon, my Lord.
You can see how long the training will take by Left-clicking the building and looking at the growing blue line.
Having learned the economic basics, it's time to learn more about building our army.
Rest up and we'll continue tomorrow.
As you can see, New Issen is coming along nicely.
If we're to protect our new town, we'll need more than one Spearman.
While you were away the townspeople built a new training building, the Target Range.
Like the Dojo, the Target Range can train Peasants into new fighters.

There are certain to be other buildings to train in, so experiment with different training combinations.
In theory you could train the fiercest of all warriors by training one peasant in three different buildings…!
It's important to have a good mix of warriors in our ranks because each type has different strengths and weaknesses.
We'll need to train different soldiers to adapt to our army to a variety of battle conditions.
This is Sparrow's Song, the bathhouse I trained in.
We Geisha are skilled in many arts, but our healing abilities are the most important to you.
To produce another Geisha, send this Peasant into the Bathhouse.
Don't be silly, of course not!

Unlike other clansmen, healers cannot enter other training buildings.

Let's rest until morning, my Lord - today's been easy enough, but tomorrow…
...Tomorrow you'll learn about combat, my most exciting lecture.

If you Left-click that you will be moved to any active battles that involve our forces.
And that fellow with the torch…it's a Raider!

Do you see the small map in the bottom right corner of the screen?

Look in the bottom left corner of the interface.

If we attack from higher ground we will surely win!

I don't have anything to say.

Between your instincts and Longtooth's wits, I'm sure our Clan will survive.

We must press our attack to the towns above!

That should take care of another barrier.

Yvaine and the corrupted totem are nothing but ashes now.

She wields the powers of a god…I don't think it'll be that easy.
I thought I was finished with filthy, Lotus-smelling caves.
You want me to share a throne with this maniac?
You'd better come back alive, Grayback.
Wait…are those Serpent troops at the bottom of the mountain?
More Serpent troops are climbing the mountain! We must reach Yvaine!
I'm telling you, Grayback's in trouble!
We've got to go after him!
But he can't do this alone! He needs us!
They don't have to be his last orders!
…I guess he didn't need us after all…
I should have gone after him…
I knew you'd make it, Lord!
He won't try soon! We must have slain half his army on this mountain.
The Totem must be very powerful to create such a storm.
Do you think Gaihla could help us, Wildeye?
If Gaihla can't stop this storm, we'll join him soon enough.
Yes, but can we trust what he's become?
Gaihla, the weather is getting worse.
Can you help us stop Yvaine's winter?
Why would any of us abandon you now, Lord Grayback?
There's no way we can fight off an army!
But how will he find us?
I'm sorry, Grayback, but you'll never win against the Lotus.
You offer us nothing but death…and Budo offered us food.
Please don't take me back to the cage!
Grayback, we thought you were dead!
Wait…there's someone approaching from the East…
Yes, it's Longtooth! And there's a whole army of Wolves behind him!
There's a small town in the southwest…I see slaves in the fields.
And there's a great fortress in the southeast, blocking a pass through the mountains.
Since Budo started ordering us around, I've hardly eaten a thing!
Do you think Mistress Yvaine is starting to trust us, Grayback?
Ha! Fighting's the easiest thing in the world!
It's pretending to be weak that's driving me crazy!
Yeah, but what about our dinner?
I can't! I'm so hungry, I'm about to fall over!
Look at this, Grayback! It's amazing!
Don't hurt us! Budo told us there was shale down here!
We didn't touch your magic stuff...promise!
This isn't an ordinary punishment, Grayback!
I have a bad feeling about this…
We heard fighting, but we couldn't open the gate!
The Lotus have a bunch of these rice bins stashed down here.
Free us, and we'll bust 'em open for you!
So the trappers were trapped, and the murderers slain!
Congratulations, Grayback, on a battle well fought!
I am both Monk and Ninja. Half Light, half Darkness.
I serve Yin and Yang, and the Balance of all things.
At the moment, the Yin of the Lotus is very strong -- it threatens the land itself.
By protecting this Monastery, I strengthen the Yang and serve the Balance.
The Monks were not harmed, and Grayback's heroes arrived safely.
I think I protected them very well!
Yvaine owes her blood to the Lord of the Wolves. It is not mine to spill.
But I am a master of roads and journeys, and I can help you reach your goal.
Listen closely, and I will give you the secrets you need…
The road to Yvaine is blocked by two magical gateways.
These are maintained by a pair of rival archmages, Issyl and Koril.
Issyl and Koril despise each other. They never cooperate on anything.
If you defeat them both quickly, you'll slip right through their gates.
But beware! If you kill only Issyl, then Koril will take control of his armies.
Likewise, Issyl would be quick to take advantage of Koril's demise.
Either way, if you let them combine their forces, you're in for a tough fight!
Now, I must depart. The Balance calls me to other lands.
Fight well, Grayback! We both have unfinished duties in this world!
Now I'll never avenge my murdered family…
Pain, eh? I could show you a thing or two about that…
Aye, it's good to see a friendly face around here.
I'm a Wolf, all right, but I've never been in those stinking mines.
My allies in the forest kept me well-hidden after the war.
The Lotus destroyed my family and my home, but they couldn't catch Wildeye!
I've been stalking and killing those devils ever since.
Are you kidding? I've waited seven years to hear those words!
You're the one who's dying today, witch!
Seven years ago, you murdered my mate and my cubs.
But you wouldn't remember that, would you?
We're too late! How could the Lotus have beaten us here?
What? Gaihla's Sanctuary has frozen over?
But Gaihla's magic has always protected her lands from the winter…
Kill you? We thought we'd turn you over to the Dryads.
They're sure they can talk you into changing your evil ways.
And they're willing to spend a long, long time doing it…
My wolves can find anything. Let's go!
He's saying the same thing my wolves tell me…that Gaihla's trail ends here.
No, the wolves would smell her blood.
Huh? Where did this Wolf Clansman come from?
I'd better stalk these two and see if they lead me to Gaihla.
Can't let them see me, or I'll never find out where they're heading!
Curses…we've lost them! Now we'll never find Gaihla!
There's nothing here. Are they mad?
Unbelievable! The Lotus have built themselves an invisible town!
I'll bet my mustache that Gaihla's down there somewhere.
You're right...what if this place disappears again?
I bet that magic tower is what makes this town invisible.
If only we could destroy it before the Lotus can use it again…
Good idea! If we roll boulders onto their buildings, they'll panic for sure!
That'll buy enough time for Grayback to hear the commotion and find us.
What in the world is that thing? It's monstrous!
Gah! We've been surrounded by more of those disgusting monsters!
We can't let them stop us…it's time to roll some rocks!
Hey, it seems to be attacking that magic tower!
What a way to go…ripped apart by a pack of midgets.
Lady Gaihla? Are you all right?
We've lost them…now we'll never find Gaihla!
A glorious battle, but there's nobody left to follow…we'll never find Gaihla now!
The town vanished again! We've lost our chance to save Gaihla!
Shouldn't get too close until Grayback arrives…I'd better just keep pushing boulders.
There's an abandoned monastery, but I have a bad feeling about that…
There's not a soul in sight, but the gardens are well-tended.
Yeah, and it's also the only shelter for miles around.
Follow me, milady…we're almost to safety.
What happened to the monks who lived here?
Gaihla is resting in the Monastery -- the Monks have promised to heal her.
But this odd fellow won't leave me alone…
But you couldn't even protect the Monks from Utara's mercenaries!
And I think you're completely mad!
Our witchcraft? This is Yvaine's work, you dunce!
I bet that pansy would run screaming from a real fight.
Let's tear down his Royal Academies…he won't be so tough without his bodyguards.
The Academies will be lightly defended, as long as we steer clear of Taro's main forces.
If we destroy all three Academies, Taro will know we mean business.
Are you stupid? Look at us! We're freezing out here!
Do you really think dirty savages like us know such powerful spells?
We're not magicians, we're miners, you dolt!
By all the gods, it's cold! I can't even feel my mustache!
What happens when we reach Yvaine? Do we just kill her?
We are not leaving you now!
Hope he knows what he's doing…
We must not dishonor Grayback's last orders.
What was that blast? We thought you were a goner!
And the other half can wait until Spring!
All hail the Lord of the Wolves!
In all my years, I've never seen a blizzard like this.
I don't mind a little snow, but this stuff is cold as death!
Ha ha! You're not the first to think so!
Not everyone who disappeared in that battle was lost, Grayback.
Gaihla is alive, and her Druidesses, too!
The woods-walkers have ways of hiding from their enemies.
They're still living in the old swamps, waiting for us to return.
She knows more of the ancient ways than any living Wolf.
If Gaihla can't figure out how to stop this nasty weather, nobody can.
He fights like a behemoth! I say we're lucky he's on our side.
That black-hearted sorceress still owes me a debt of blood. I'm coming.
And we'll fight by your side until the end.
